The Independent — published Wednesday 30 September 2026, 06:00 BST (David Hughes)

Cooper pledges revival of 'one of Labour's greatest achievements' - Sure Start
The Health Secretary will announce support for babies and parents will be expanded through a network of local hubs.

Yvette Cooper will signal a revival of the New Labour-era Sure Start scheme, with new parents getting support with their babies at more than 1,000 centres across England by 2028.

The Health Secretary will set out the plan as Labour's conference in Liverpool draws to a close.

The Health Secretary will set out the expansion of the Healthy Babies programme to all local authority areas to revive the Sure Start principle of an integrated approach to supporting families.

The plan - dubbed "Sure Start 2.0" by aides - will see parents get enhanced infant feeding and mental health support, help to form strong relationships with their babies along with contact with health visitors and midwives.

Ms Cooper is expected to say: "Since the election, Bridget Phillipson and Lucy Powell have been working to rebuild family hubs across the country, bringing back support for parents and for young children.
"But something is missing. In half of communities, compared to the last time round, the healthy babies services - mental health support for mums and dad, the feeding and bonding support for your new baby.
"That changes now.
"I can announce we will bring back the Sure Start health services into every family centre.
"Reaching up to 1,000 hubs over the next two years.
"One of the Labour Party's greatest achievements restored to families throughout the land."
